terms.meaning: The basic material historians use to build an account of the past, such as tools, coins, buildings and writings.
Written works from a period. They are of two kinds: native and foreign.
Physical remains found by research and digging: inscriptions, coins, monuments, pots and other ruins.
The study of how coins began and developed.
A surviving building that shows our cultural heritage, such as a temple, stupa, palace or fort.
Digging out buried remains using scientific methods.
Poems, songs and ballads passed down by word of mouth. They help us know local history.
A legend about a place, usually a religious one. It shows beliefs more than direct history.

items.name: Native literature
items.formula: Written by Indians, in any Indian language with a written form.
items.example: Kautilya: Arthashastra. Kalhana: Rajatarangini. Banabhatta: Harsha Charitha. Pampa: Vikramarjuna Vijaya.

items.name: More native works and their authors
items.formula: Ashwaghosha: Buddha Charita. Vishakadatta: Mudrarakshasa. Hala: Gathasaptashati.
items.example: Srivijaya: Kavirajamarga. Chand Bardayi: Prithviraja Raso.

items.name: Foreign literature
items.formula: Written by foreign writers, travellers and scholars.
items.example: Megasthenes: Indica. Huien Tsang: Si-Yu-Ki. Fa-Hien: Gho-Kho-Ki. Ptolemy: Geography.

items.name: Foreign sources on Sri Lanka and Vijayanagara
items.formula: Ceylon gives us Deepavamsha and Mahavamsha.
items.example: Nuniz, Barbosa and Nicolo Conti wrote about the Vijayanagar Empire.

items.name: What inscriptions tell us
items.formula: Religion, culture, economy and administration of their time.
items.example: The earliest in India are Emperor Ashoka's, on rocks and stone pillars.

items.name: Ashoka's inscriptions
items.formula: Mostly in Brahmi and Kharoshti scripts, in the Prakrit language. Some are in Greek and Aramaic.
items.example: In Karnataka they were found at Maski and Brahmagiri.

items.name: First Kannada inscription
items.example: It belongs to the reign of Kakutsavarma of the Kadamba dynasty.

items.name: Other inscriptions and their kings
items.formula: Allahabad Pillar: Samudra Gupta. Aihole: Pulikeshi II. Hathigumpa: Kharavela.

items.name: What coins tell us
items.formula: They show the king's power, and also the religion, culture and economy of the time.
items.example: Samudra Gupta issued 7 types of gold coins.

items.name: Roman coins in Bengaluru
items.formula: They prove this region traded with the Romans.
items.example: That trade was about 2000 years ago.

items.name: Monuments that show science and technology
items.formula: Mehrauli's Iron Pillar and the Whispering Gallery of Gol Gumbaz.

items.name: What excavations revealed
items.formula: Bhimbetka and Sanganakallu: Stone Age culture.
items.example: Harappa and Mohenjodaro: the Indus Valley Civilization.

items.name: Carbon-14 dating
items.formula: Used only on remains of living things. After death C-12 stays constant while C-14 falls, halving in 5700 years.
items.example: After 11400 years, a quarter of the C-14 is left.

items.name: People remembered in oral literature
items.formula: The Nayakas of Chitradurga, Kempegowda, Tippu Sultan, Sangolli Rayanna and Kitturu Rani Chennamma.
items.example: Tribes and communities without writing kept their experiences this way.

mistakes.text: C-14 dating does not work on stone or metal, because it is only for remains of things that once lived.
Coins and inscriptions are archaeological sources even though they carry writing. Literary sources are written works.
A Sthala-Purana is not direct history. It shows what people believed about a place.
